segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Hi Alex. It’s Martha Clines here. James White gave me your number. I hope you don’t mind me calling you.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Of course not. How are you, Martha?

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Good thanks. I’m ringing because I need a bit of advice.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Oh yeah. What about?

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: The training you did at JPNW a few years ago. I’m applying for the same thing.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Oh right. Yes, I did mine in 2014 . Best thing I ever did. I’m still working there.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Really? What are you doing?

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Well, now I work in the customer services department but I did my initial training in Finance [[ ]] . I stayed there for the first two years and then moved to where I am now.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: That’s the same department I’m applying for. Did you enjoy it?

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: I was pretty nervous to begin with. I didn’t do well in my exams at school and I was really worried because I failed Maths [[ ]] . But it didn’t actually matter because I did lots of courses on the job.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Did you get a diploma at the end of your trainee period? I’m hoping to do the one in business skills.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Yes. That sounds good. I took the one on IT skills but I wish I’d done that one instead. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: OK, that’s good to know. What about the other trainees? How did you get on with them?

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: There were about 20 of us who started at the same time and we were all around the same age – I was 18 and there was only one person younger than me, how was 17 [[ ]] . The rest were between 18 and 20. I made some good friends.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: I’ve heard lots of good things about the training at JPNW. It seems like there are a lot of opportunities there.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Yeah, definitely. Because of its size you can work in loads of different areas within the organisation.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: What about pay? I know you get a lower minimum wage than regular employees.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: That’s right – which isn’t great. But you get the same number of days’ holiday as everyone else [[ ]] . And the pay goes up massively if they offer you a job at the end of the training period.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Yeah, but I’m not doing it for the money – it’s the experience I think will be really useful. Everyone says by the end of the year you gain so much confidence.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: You’re right. That’s the most useful part about it. There’s a lot of variety too. You’re given lots of different things to do. I enjoyed it all – I didn’t even mind the studying.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Do you have to spend any time in college?

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Yes, one day each month [[ ]] . So you get lots of support from both your tutor and your manager.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: That’s good. And the company is easy to get to, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Yes, it’s very close to the train station so the location’s a real advantage. [[ ]] ———————-

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Have you got a date for your interview yet?

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Yes, it’s on the 23rd of this month.

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: So long as you’re well prepared there’s nothing to worry about. Everyone’s very friendly.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: I am not sure what I should wear. What do you think?

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Nothing too casual – like jeans [[ ]] , for example. If you’ve got a nice jacket, wear that with a skirt or trousers.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: OK. Thanks. Any other tips?

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Erm, well I know it’s really obvious but arrive in plenty of time [[ ]] . They hate people who are late. So make sure you know exactly where you have to get to. And one other useful piece of advice my manager told me before I had the interview for this job – is to smile [[ ]] . Even if you feel terrified. It makes people respond better to you.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: I’ll have to practise doing that in the mirror!

segments.speaker: ALEX
segments.en: Yeah – well, good luck. Let me know if you need any more information.

segments.speaker: MARTHA
segments.en: Thanks very much.
